title: Netflix and Kill
victoryHeadline: Caught! Someone's getting an ending nobody asked for.
acts: Movie night at Vaughn's had, by eight o'clock, produced no movie. Austin was elbow-deep in the living-room shelf, pulling out DVDs for a player the house hadn't owned in six years and insisting each one was basically still watchable on a laptop that didn't have a drive either. Charlotte had claimed the one chair that didn't creak and had spent twenty minutes daring anyone, with just her eyebrows, to suggest she give it up. Enid stood by the TV working through a universal remote with three dead batteries already discarded on the carpet, entirely convinced the fourth one in her pocket was the one that would finally do it. In the kitchen, mercifully out of range of all three of them, Dean had a set of scales out and was weighing portions off a sourdough starter he'd been quietly nursing for four months and had never once mentioned to anyone in this house.

"The wifi password's on a sticky note somewhere in my desk," Vaughn called through from the bedroom, on his knees beside a chair buried in laundry he kept meaning to fold, going through drawer after drawer. Barbara wandered in after him, phone in hand, and settled on the end of the bed to wait it out. "Take your time," she said, "it's not like anything's happening out there." This was, at that moment, almost true — the living room had reached the kind of pitch where Austin's DVD case, Charlotte's chair, and Enid's remote were all being argued about simultaneously, loud enough that a much smaller sound from down the hall wouldn't have stood a chance. Dean, three rooms and one very precise set of scales away, didn't hear anything either.

It was Dean who eventually carried the popcorn through, took one look at the empty end of the sofa, and asked where Vaughn had got to with that password. Nobody had a good answer. The bedroom door was ajar. The sticky note, it turned out, had been on the desk the whole time — face up, easy to find, completely unread.

whereabouts.A: Austin was elbow-deep in the shelf, working through a stack of DVDs for a player the house hadn't owned in six years, insisting each one was basically still watchable on a laptop with no disc drive either.
whereabouts.B: Barbara stayed curled up on the end of the bed, phone in hand, keeping Vaughn company while he hunted for a wifi password he swore was somewhere obvious.
whereabouts.C: Charlotte had claimed the one chair in the living room that didn't creak, and had spent the last twenty minutes daring anyone, with just her eyebrows, to suggest she give it up.
whereabouts.D: Dean stood at the kitchen counter with a set of scales, weighing out portions of a sourdough starter he'd been nursing for four months and had never once mentioned to anyone in this house.
whereabouts.E: Enid worked through every button on a universal remote with three dead batteries already on the carpet, convinced the fourth one in her pocket was the one that would finally do it.
whereabouts.V: Vaughn was on his knees beside a chair buried in laundry, working through drawer after drawer for a wifi password sticky note that had to be in there somewhere.

reveal: It was Barbara, in the bedroom, on the very bed she'd spent the evening curled up on. While Vaughn dug through his desk for a password he never found, she reached for the pillow beside her instead. The living room's three-way argument over DVDs, chairs, and remote batteries covered the ten quiet minutes that followed; Dean's scales, three rooms away, covered the rest. She was back on the sofa's arm before the popcorn finished popping, one dead battery away from a house that never thought to ask her anything.

escape.generic: The sticky note is still on that desk, face up, easy to find. Nobody ever did agree on a movie, and somewhere out there the real killer already knows which remote button works.

byAccused.A: Austin was led out mid-sentence, one hand still full of DVDs nobody owns a player for, complaining that rejecting a movie is not, legally, a crime.
byAccused.C: Charlotte's chair sat empty for the rest of the night — nobody else in the house had the nerve to sit in it, guilty or not.
byAccused.D: The others found Dean's sourdough starter in the fridge two days later, still alive, with nobody quite sure whose job it now was to feed it.
byAccused.E: Enid's own verdict, delivered loudly to the arresting officer, was that the fourth battery would definitely have worked, and no one would ever know now.
